items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: The name 'Dan' appears only in the phrase 'as Dan --', which functions as a vocative address to the interviewer or a filler, with no description of a personal or professional relationship between the interviewee (Charles Thompson) and a person named Dan.

ctx.x: Right. One other thing I'd like to ask you about Hamp. Hamp's talents for improvisation and his knowledge of chord progressions and what not, I mean he's an extremely experienced musician, is he not?

Well, I always said, and I say this still now, I have never -- I've played with all the musicians that you can name, practically, that were jazz musicians in my life time, and I've never played with anyone more talented on the drums or the vibraphones than Lionel. And of course

he can play that piano with those two fingers, and get a lot of music out of it. And he's -- the man is incredible, he's just a natural born genius as a player, as a player. There's no doubt in my mind, as Dan -- and I would also have to say that I learned more from him than I had from anyone else as far as playing music is because before that I had been primarily an arranger.
